- Pool depth is only 87.8 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces the high end of the 1.4-5.1% cost band, and a stop at 20% can slip well past its level in a thin pool.

memos.scout:
The strongest honest case: the coin is classed ORGANIC, not factory or operator-backed. There was no airdrop dump, the curve is spread across 211 buyers with top-3 holding only 8.6%, and the 30-minute return is +26%. Over the last 15 minutes, buyers (244) outnumbered sellers (198), buy SOL (187.9) exceeded sell SOL (152.4), and net flow was +35.5 SOL on about $42k volume. The coin is still alive at roughly $53k market cap.

The case is weak, though. Post-graduation sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 0.97, meaning early buyers largely exited, and the coin is 61% off its 30-minute high, so the recent rally is a rebound from a sharp drop, not a trend. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% at a $20 ticket eat into any small move, and a launch bot was present. I see no clear evidence that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. Recommendation: skip, or at most a very small position with a tight exit plan.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a dump after the late run-up. RICH is up 142% over the last 15 minutes (return 1.4192), yet it sits 61% below its 30-minute high, so it has already round-tripped sharply. In the first two minutes after graduation, sells nearly matched buys (sell_to_buy 0.97) and the top 5 buyers took 30% of flow, a sign of early holders taking profit into the bid. Last 15 minutes show net flow of only +35 SOL on 188 SOL bought against 152 sold, with 198 sellers, so momentum is fading. The curve shows a 27% bundle share and a 20% completer share, which suggests coordinated early entry. With a $20 ticket and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a 88 SOL pool, a modest 5-10% pullback would wipe out any gain. Skip.
